summary: Janice Dean Willis is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees at Cornell and a PhD at Columbia under Alex Wayman. She held posts at Wesleyan University (Professor, 1977–2013) and Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Janice Leoshko works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Janine Schotmans is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ludo Rocher. She served as curator of the Indian section at the Royal Museums of Art and History.

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David Germano. He held a post at the University of Virginia (attested 2007).

Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, completing his dissertation by 1985, and also studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Uppsala University and studied at the University of Bonn. He spent his career at Uppsala University, becoming Assistant Professor (1908), Deputy Professor (1925), and Professor (1927).

Jaromír Borecký (1869–1951) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague (~1888–1893). He served as Director of the National Library of the Czech Republic (~1920–1935).
Jaromír Jedlička (1869–1901) specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at Charles University under Josef Zubatý (1888–1894) and worked as a library worker there in 1899.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a sinologist who studied at Charles University's Faculty of Arts from around 1924 to 1928.
Jaroslav Strnad is an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Charles University (~1974–1979). He held a post at the Czech Academy of Sciences around 1989.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. His posts include Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (2015–2024) and Research Associate at Oxford (2024).

Jason Hawkes is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Cambridge. He held positions including Project Curator at the British Museum (2014–2020), Lecturer at Cambridge (2017–2019), and Visiting Professor at Leiden University (2021).
Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki. He became a Professor at Seattle University in 2005.
Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen. He subsequently served as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon. He held posts at the University of Florida (2003–2010) and Wilfrid Laurier University (2010).

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning a PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick. He has held appointments as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.
Jason Schwartz is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. As of 2026, he is attested as a Lecturer at Stanford University and Curator at the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute.

Javana Ñāṇa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the National University of Mongolia, ITBMU, Shan State Buddhist University, and the University of Kelaniya. He served as a Bhikkhu at Shan State Buddhist University in 2025.

Jay Holt Valentine is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He was appointed Associate Professor at Troy University in 2015.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard under Calvert Watkins. He held professorships at UC Berkeley (~1969–1972), Cornell (1981–1985), and Harvard, where he became Diebold Professor in 1998.
